newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada minister uses government plastic to buy fur.
newsitem.headline: Canada minister uses government plastic to buy fur.

text.p: A junior Canadian minister on Thursday admitted that she used a government credit card to pay a deposit on a fur coat.
Ethel Blondin-Andrew, secretary of state for training and youth, said she repaid the deposit and while she had used "poor judgment" she declined to leave office as the Reform Party had demanded.
"My use of government credit cards for personal purchases was a mistake and in poor judgment," she told Parliament.

Reform, the third largest party in the House of Commons, has been pursuing the government of Liberal Prime Minister Jean Chretien. Three other ministers have had to leave under a cloud in his three years.

The Toronto Sun uncovered her irregularities under the Access to Information Act, receiving copies of her expense claims in which she certified "that the foregoing expenses have been incurred on official business."

Much of each claim had been blanked out on the grounds they contained personal information. Blondin-Andrew said she had accompanied her expense submissions with a check to cover the personal portion and no one in bureaucracy had questioned her open use of the American Express and Diners Club cards for personal purchases.
Chretien told Parliament: "I am satisfied that the secretary of state acted in good faith all along."

His Liberals relentlessly attacked Conservative former Prime Minister Brian Mulroney on charges of corruption and Chretien had until recently trumpeted his success in not losing ministers under questionable circumstances.

Reform member Deborah Grey charged on Wednesday that he had broken a campaign promise by not appointing an ethics counsellor who reports directly to Parliament and pressured him to publish the cabinet ethics guidelines he has set.
